foodie.title: A Bifana at O Trevo
foodie.description: A tiny counter on Praça Luís de Camões serving marinated pork in a bread roll, eaten standing, for the price of a coffee.
foodie.bonus: Have it with a bica at the same counter.

foodie.title: Manteigaria, Straight Off the Tray
foodie.description: Stand at the marble counter in Chiado and eat a pastel de nata still too hot to hold, with cinnamon shaken over the top.
foodie.bonus: Wait for the bell that means a fresh tray is out.

foodie.title: Two Stars at Belcanto
foodie.description: José Avillez's Chiado dining room, where Portuguese classics get rebuilt into something you have to be told the name of to recognise.
foodie.bonus: Take the tasting menu, not the à la carte.

foodie.title: Coffee at Fábrica Coffee Roasters
foodie.description: Portugal roasts its own beans dark and bitter; this is the place that decided to do the opposite, and it changed Lisbon's coffee.
foodie.bonus: Order a bica and a filter and taste them back to back.

foodie.title: Dinner at Taberna Sal Grosso
foodie.description: Twenty seats in Alfama doing serious, modern Portuguese cooking at prices that make no sense for how good it is.
foodie.bonus: Book weeks ahead. There is no walk-in option.

foodie.title: Petiscos at Taberna da Rua das Flores
foodie.description: A no-bookings former grocery with a handwritten menu that changes daily and a queue outside from the moment it opens.
foodie.bonus: Put your name down, go for a drink, come back.

foodie.title: Garlic Prawns at Cervejaria Ramiro
foodie.description: A loud, tiled beer hall in Intendente where you work through shellfish by weight and finish, correctly, with a steak sandwich for dessert.
foodie.bonus: The prego at the end is not optional.

foodie.title: Portuguese Wine Under a Bottle Ceiling
foodie.description: A Chiado wine bar in a vaulted room lined entirely with bottles, pouring Portuguese producers by the glass with cheese and presunto to match.
foodie.bonus: Drink something from the Alentejo you have never heard of.

foodie.title: Pastéis de Belém, Fresh from the Oven
foodie.description: Line up at the original 1837 bakery for a custard tart so good it gave the whole category its name.
foodie.bonus: Eat it standing at the counter, still warm

foodie.title: Ginjinha at the Counter of A Ginjinha
foodie.description: Order a tiny glass of sour-cherry liqueur at the doorway-sized bar that has been pouring it on Largo de São Domingos since 1840, then drink it standing in the square.
foodie.bonus: Ask for it 'com elas' — with the cherries

foodie.title: Graze Time Out Market
foodie.description: Sample stalls from some of Lisbon's best chefs under one roof at this converted market hall.

foodie.title: Tinned Fish and Wine at Sol e Pesca
foodie.description: An old fishing-tackle shop in Cais do Sodré turned bar, where dinner is a wall of Portuguese tins opened at your table with bread and a glass of white.
foodie.bonus: Order whatever the catch of the day is, no menu-scanning

social.title: Drinks at Pensão Amor
social.description: A former dockside brothel off Cais do Sodré turned into a gloriously overdecorated bar, with an erotica bookshop on the way to the toilets.
social.bonus: Find the room with the painted ceiling.

social.title: Craft Beer at Cerveteca Lisboa
social.description: A small Príncipe Real bar that was pouring Portuguese craft beer before there was much of it, with tables spilling onto the square outside.
social.bonus: Ask for the most Portuguese thing on tap.

social.title: Fado Vadio at Tasca do Jaime
social.description: Amateur fado in a Graça back room on a weekend afternoon, where locals take turns singing and the whole place goes silent for each one.
social.bonus: Stay for at least four singers before you leave.

social.title: Benfica at the Estádio da Luz
social.description: Sixty-five thousand people, a live eagle flying a lap before kick-off, and a noise level that makes conversation pointless.
social.bonus: Be in your seat for the eagle. That is the whole point.

social.title: Kiosk Drinks in Príncipe Real
social.description: Sit under the enormous 150-year-old cedar in the garden square with a beer from the kiosk while the whole neighbourhood does the same.
social.bonus: Stay until the lights come on in the trees.

social.title: Lux Frágil Until Sunrise
social.description: Lisbon's serious club, in a riverside warehouse with a rooftop terrace where everyone ends up watching the sun come over the Tagus.
social.bonus: Do not arrive before 2am and do not leave before 6.

social.title: Rooftop at Topo Chiado
social.description: A terrace bar hidden on top of a shopping centre, looking straight across at the roofless arches of the Carmo Convent.
social.bonus: Get there before sunset to claim a rail spot.

social.title: Santo António: Sardines in the Streets
social.description: On the night of 12 June every alley in Alfama fills with grills, paper decorations, cheap wine and the marchas populares parading down the avenue.
social.bonus: Eat a grilled sardine on bread, standing in the street.

social.title: Fado Night at Tasca do Chico
social.description: Squeeze into a packed Bairro Alto tasca for raw, unamplified fado, Portugal's soul music, sung inches from your table.
social.bonus: Stay silent during the song, like the regulars do

social.title: Rooftop Drinks at Park Bar
social.description: Ride a parking-garage elevator up to a hidden rooftop bar with one of the best sunset views in the city.
social.bonus: Get there before sunset to grab a rail spot

social.title: Pink Street Night Out
social.description: Dance through Cais do Sodré's famous pink-paved strip of bars and clubs that runs until sunrise.
social.bonus: Try the pink-cobblestone dance floor at least once

social.title: Bar Hopping Bairro Alto
social.description: Join the nightly street party as Bairro Alto's tiny bars spill their crowds out onto the cobblestones.
social.bonus: Take your drink to the street with everyone else

culture.title: Opera at São Carlos
culture.description: A gilded 1793 horseshoe theatre in Chiado, built to replace the opera house the earthquake destroyed, still the best room in the city for sound.
culture.bonus: Dress for it. Everyone else will.

culture.title: The National Tile Museum
culture.description: Five centuries of azulejo inside a former convent, ending with a 23-metre panorama of Lisbon painted before the 1755 earthquake flattened it.
culture.bonus: Find the pre-earthquake panorama and pick out what is gone.

culture.title: The Gulbenkian and Its Garden
culture.description: One man's private collection — Egyptian, Islamic, Rembrandt, and a whole room of Lalique — in a modernist building set in its own park.
culture.bonus: Find the Lalique room and give it proper time.

culture.title: The Museu do Fado in Alfama
culture.description: The history of saudade set to music — listening booths, guitars, and the story of how a dockside song became the national one.
culture.bonus: Sit in a booth and listen to Amália properly before you go out to a fado house.

culture.title: The Bosch Triptych at the MNAA
culture.description: Portugal's national collection holds Bosch's Temptations of St. Anthony — a wall of nightmares in a quiet room almost nobody queues for.
culture.bonus: Give the triptych fifteen minutes and keep finding things.

culture.title: MAAT and the Wave You Can Walk On
culture.description: A low white tiled building on the Belém waterfront whose roof you climb and walk over, with contemporary art and a power station underneath.
culture.bonus: Walk the roof at sunset even if the galleries are shut.

culture.title: The Roofless Convent do Carmo
culture.description: Gothic arches open to the sky, left exactly as the 1755 earthquake dropped them, in the middle of the city as a deliberate memorial.
culture.bonus: Go at midday when the light comes straight down through the arches.

culture.title: Inside the Torre de Belém
culture.description: The Manueline watchtower that ships left from and returned to, with stone rope carved round it and a rhinoceros on one corner.
culture.bonus: Go early — the spiral stair works on a one-way traffic light.

chill.title: Ferry to Cacilhas for the Sunset Back
chill.description: Ten minutes across the water to a working ferry town, a walk along the old warehouses, and the best view of Lisbon on the boat home.
chill.bonus: Sit on the top deck coming back, facing the city.

chill.title: LX Factory and Ler Devagar
chill.description: A converted industrial complex under the bridge, with a bookshop built inside an old printing press and a flying bicycle hanging over it.
chill.bonus: Go on a Sunday for the market in the alley.

chill.title: The Estufa Fria Greenhouse
chill.description: A cool, shaded glasshouse at the top of Parque Eduardo VII with streams, palms and almost nobody in it on a weekday.
chill.bonus: Find the hot house and the sweet house too.

chill.title: An Afternoon in Cerca da Graça
chill.description: A walled hillside park above Mouraria with olive trees, a kiosk and a castle view, used almost entirely by people who live there.
chill.bonus: Buy something from the kiosk and stay two hours.

chill.title: The Tropical Botanical Garden in Belém
chill.description: Palms, banyans and roaming peacocks in a walled colonial-era garden that almost every visitor to Belém walks straight past.
chill.bonus: Find the avenue of palms and walk the length of it.

chill.title: Tiles and Terraces at Santa Luzia
chill.description: A pergola-covered terrace in Alfama with blue azulejo panels on the wall and the whole tiled rooftop tumble running down to the river.
chill.bonus: Walk on to Portas do Sol and compare the two views.

chill.title: Wander Jerónimos Monastery Cloisters
chill.description: Walk the limestone cloisters of a UNESCO monastery built to celebrate Portugal's age of exploration.
chill.bonus: Find the quietest corner of the cloister and just sit

chill.title: Sunset at Miradouro da Senhora do Monte
chill.description: Claim Lisbon's highest viewpoint at golden hour and watch the entire city turn orange below you.
chill.bonus: Bring a bottle of vinho verde and share it

chill.title: Ride the Historic Tram 28
chill.description: Rattle through Lisbon's steepest, narrowest streets aboard the century-old yellow tram that locals still ride to work.
chill.bonus: Sit by the window and just watch the city go by

chill.title: Afternoon at Miradouro de Santa Catarina
chill.description: Post up at this laid-back terrace overlooking the river, a local hangout with cheap beer and street musicians.
chill.bonus: People-watch for a full hour, phone away

8ball.title: Take Any Tram to the End of the Line
8ball.description: Get on the first tram that stops, stay on past every place you recognise, and spend the afternoon in whatever neighbourhood it abandons you in.
8ball.bonus: Eat lunch within two streets of where you get off.

8ball.title: Follow the Sound of Fado
8ball.description: Walk into Alfama after dark with no destination and keep turning toward whichever doorway the guitar is coming from until you find a room worth staying in.
8ball.bonus: Go into the third place you hear, not the first.

adventure.title: Cycle the Cascais to Guincho Coast Path
adventure.description: A flat seafront track from Cascais out to the dunes and surf of Guincho, riding straight into the Atlantic wind the whole way.
adventure.bonus: Ride out into the headwind so you get the tailwind home.

adventure.title: Stand at the Westernmost Point of Europe
adventure.description: Cabo da Roca is a cliff at the end of the continent, with nothing between you and Newfoundland but grey Atlantic and a lot of wind.
adventure.bonus: Walk south along the clifftop path away from the car park.

adventure.title: Sail the Tagus at Golden Hour
adventure.description: Take a small sailboat out of the Belém docks and see the tower, the bridge and the whole tiled waterfront from the water as the light drops.
adventure.bonus: Ask to take the tiller for ten minutes.

adventure.title: The Abandoned Viewpoint at Monsanto
adventure.description: Walk up through Lisbon's forest park to the Panorâmico de Monsanto, a derelict sixties restaurant now covered in graffiti with a 360-degree view.
adventure.bonus: Go all the way up to the top terrace.

adventure.title: Surf Ericeira, a World Surfing Reserve
adventure.description: Forty-five minutes north to a fishing town with seven world-class breaks in a few kilometres, and lessons for whichever one suits you.
adventure.bonus: Eat at the harbour afterwards with salt still in your hair.

adventure.title: Ferry to Almada and Climb to Cristo Rei
adventure.description: Cross the Tagus from Cais do Sodré, then go up the arms-outstretched statue on the far bank for the view back at the whole city and its bridge.
adventure.bonus: Take the ferry rather than the bridge, both ways.

adventure.title: Hike the Serra da Arrábida to a Hidden Beach
adventure.description: A limestone ridge an hour south drops into water the colour of the Caribbean. Walk down to Galapinhos and swim off the sand.
adventure.bonus: Get in the water even if nobody else does.

adventure.title: Watch the Giants at Nazaré
adventure.description: Stand on the fort at Praia do Norte in winter and watch tow-in surfers drop into waves the height of an office block.
adventure.bonus: Check the swell forecast and go on the biggest day of your trip.

adventure.title: Explore the Alfama's Hidden Stairways
adventure.description: Get lost on purpose in Lisbon's oldest neighborhood, a maze of tiled stairways, laundry lines, and hidden viewpoints.
adventure.bonus: Take a staircase you've never seen before

adventure.title: Bike the Riverfront to Belém
adventure.description: Pedal the flat riverside path from downtown out to the monuments of Belém, river on one side the whole way.
adventure.bonus: Ride all the way to the Belém Tower and back

adventure.title: Climb São Jorge Castle Walls
adventure.description: Climb the ancient walls of Lisbon's hilltop castle for a 360° view stretching from the Tagus to the rooftops of Alfama.
adventure.bonus: Walk the full length of the ramparts

adventure.title: Sunrise Run Through Eduardo VII Park
adventure.description: Run the sloped lawns of Lisbon's grand central park as the city wakes up around you.
adventure.bonus: Run to the top terrace and catch your breath at the view

adventure.title: Day Trip to Sintra's Pena Palace
adventure.description: Take the train into the hills to explore a candy-colored 19th-century palace perched above a fog-shrouded forest.
adventure.bonus: Climb to the very top turret

adventure.title: Paddleboard the Flatwater at Marina de Oeiras
adventure.description: Twenty minutes down the coast line, push a board out of the marina onto glassy water and paddle past the 16th-century sea forts toward Santo Amaro.
adventure.bonus: Try to make it out to the marina and back

adventure.title: A First Surf Lesson at Costa da Caparica
adventure.description: Cross the river to Lisbon's closest surf beach and get two hours of Atlantic beach-break coaching with a school that puts the board under you.
adventure.bonus: Paddle out for one more wave than you planned
